Root Cause Analysis

Agri App — Docker Deployment Issues: Authentication Failures, Database Migration Gaps, Multilingual Rendering, and Language Control Logic

📅 2026-07-11 🏷️ Flutter · FastAPI · Docker · Nginx · SQLite · Alembic 👤 SOLO Analysis

Executive Summary

This report documents the root causes of four interconnected issues encountered during the Docker-based deployment of the Agri App (Flutter web frontend + FastAPI backend). Each issue manifested at a different layer of the stack — networking, database schema, frontend rendering, and application logic — but shared a common theme: configuration drift between development assumptions and containerized reality.

Issue Symptom Root Cause Resolution
401 Unauthorized All API calls from Flutter web returned 401 Frontend baseUrl pointed to localhost:8000 (frontend nginx) instead of backend Nginx reverse proxy with relative API paths
500 Internal Server Error Chat endpoints crashed with sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: conversations.status Database schema out of sync — pending Alembic migration not applied Run alembic upgrade head in backend container
Empty boxes (□□□) in chat Hindi/Tamil responses rendered as empty squares Flutter web default font lacks glyphs for Indic scripts Global fontFamilyFallback with Noto Sans fonts
Language control Assistant always replied in user's detected language No explicit language parameter passed to LLM; auto-detection only Add responseLanguage param from UI picker through full stack

Issue 1 — 401 Unauthorized on All API Calls

Observed Symptom

Docker logs showed repeated 401 Unauthorized responses for every API request from the Flutter web client. The /auth/me endpoint, chat endpoints, and farm endpoints all failed identically.

Initial Hypothesis

The team initially suspected JWT token issues — expired tokens, malformed headers, or authentication middleware misconfiguration.

Actual Root Cause

The root cause was a networking misconfiguration in the Flutter ApiService. The baseUrl was configured as:

frontend/lib/services/api_service.dart (before) 
static String get baseUrl => kIsWeb ? 'http://localhost:8000/api/v1' : 'http://192.168.0.199:8000/api/v1';

In the Docker Compose environment:

  • Frontend runs in an Nginx container on port 80 (mapped to host 3000)
  • Backend runs in a FastAPI container on port 8000 (internal only)
  • localhost:8000 from the browser resolves to the frontend Nginx container, not the backend
  • Nginx serves static Flutter files for all non-proxied paths, returning 200 OK with index.html for /api/v1/*
  • The Flutter app parsed the HTML as JSON, failed to extract a token, and sent unauthenticated requests
Key Insight

The 401 was a cascading failure: the request never reached the backend authentication middleware. It terminated at the frontend Nginx with an HTML response that the client couldn't parse.

Why the Mobile Path Worked

The mobile configuration used 192.168.0.199:8000 (the host machine's LAN IP), which correctly routed to the backend container's published port. This masked the issue during mobile testing.

Resolution

Two-phase fix to avoid full image rebuilds:

Phase 1: Docker-internal DNS (required rebuild)

api_service.dart 
static String get baseUrl => 'http://agriapp-backend-1:8000/api/v1';

Phase 2: Nginx reverse proxy (no rebuild)

Created nginx.conf.dev with API proxying:

frontend/nginx.conf.dev 
location /api/v1/ {
    proxy_pass http://agriapp-backend-1:8000/api/v1/;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

Updated docker-compose.dev.yml to mount the dev config and source code:

docker-compose.dev.yml (excerpt) 
frontend:
  image: agriapp-frontend:dev
  volumes:
    - ./frontend:/app
    - ./frontend/nginx.conf.dev:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
  ports:
    - "3000:80"
  depends_on:
    - backend

Changed frontend baseUrl to empty string for relative paths:

api_service.dart (final) 
static String get baseUrl => '';  // Relative URLs via nginx proxy

Issue 2 — 500 Internal Server Error: Missing Database Column

Observed Symptom

After fixing authentication, chat endpoints returned 500 Internal Server Error. Backend logs showed:

Backend logs 
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: conversations.status
  File "/app/app/chat/service.py", line 45, in create_pending
    db.commit()
  File "/app/app/models/conversation.py", line 22, in __init__
    self.status = status

Root Cause

The SQLAlchemy model Conversation (in backend/app/models/conversation.py) defined a status column and an error_message column that were added in migration 0002_conversation_processing_status.py. However, the migration had never been applied to the SQLite database inside the Docker container.

Why This Happened

The Docker Compose setup mounted a named volume for the database (backend_data:/app/data). On first run, Alembic created the initial schema (migration 0001). The second migration was generated locally but not included in the Docker image and not run on container startup. The container started with an outdated schema.

Schema Evolution

Migration Revision Changes Applied in Docker?
Initial 0001_initial users, farms, crops, conversations (id, user_id, farm_id, crop_id, title, created_at) ✅ Yes (auto on first run)
Processing status 0002_conversation_processing_status ADD COLUMN status, ADD COLUMN error_message, ADD COLUMN context_snapshot ❌ No — missing from container

Resolution

Executed the pending migration inside the running backend container:

Command 
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec backend alembic upgrade head

Output confirmed application:

Result 
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Context impl SQLiteImpl.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Will assume transactional DDL.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Running upgrade 0001_initial -> 0002_conversation_processing_status, conversation processing status

Prevention

Add migration execution to the backend container's entrypoint or Dockerfile CMD:

Dockerfile.backend (recommended addition) 
CMD alembic upgrade head && uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Issue 3 — Empty Boxes (□□□) in Chat Bubbles

Observed Symptom

When the AI assistant responded in Hindi (Devanagari) or Tamil, the chat bubbles displayed empty square characters (□□□) instead of proper glyphs. English text rendered correctly.

Root Cause

Flutter web's default font stack (Roboto / system fonts) lacks glyph coverage for Indic scripts. When the text shaping engine encounters a codepoint without a glyph in the primary font, it falls back through the font family. On Flutter web (CanvasKit/WASM), the fallback chain is minimal and does not include Noto fonts by default.

Platform Difference

This issue is specific to Flutter Web. Mobile (Android/iOS) and desktop builds include broader system font fallbacks that typically cover Devanagari and Tamil. The bug only surfaced in the browser deployment.

Font Coverage Analysis

Script Unicode Block Example Roboto Coverage Noto Sans Coverage
Devanagari (Hindi) U+0900–U+097F नमस्ते ❌ None ✅ Complete
Tamil U+0B80–U+0BFF வணக்கம் ❌ None ✅ Complete
Latin (English) U+0000–U+007F Hello ✅ Complete ✅ Complete

Resolution

Added a global fontFamilyFallback chain to the app's text theme in app_theme.dart:

frontend/lib/core/theme/app_theme.dart 
static const List multilingualFontFallback = [
  'Noto Sans Devanagari',
  'Noto Sans Tamil',
  'Noto Sans Bengali',
  'Noto Sans Gujarati',
  'Noto Sans Gurmukhi',
  'Noto Sans Kannada',
  'Noto Sans Malayalam',
];

static ThemeData get lightTheme {
  final base = ThemeData.light(useMaterial3: true);
  return base.copyWith(
    textTheme: _applyFallbacks(base.textTheme),
    inputDecorationTheme: base.inputDecorationTheme.copyWith(
      // Apply to TextFields too
    ),
  );
}

static TextTheme _applyFallbacks(TextTheme theme) {
  return theme.apply(
    fontFamilyFallback: multilingualFontFallback,
    displayColor: Colors.black87,
    bodyColor: Colors.black87,
  );
}

Applied the same fallback to chat bubble text styles in assistant_screen.dart:

assistant_screen.dart (chat bubble) 
Text(
  message.text,
  style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodyMedium?.copyWith(
    fontFamilyFallback: AppTheme.multilingualFontFallback,
    height: 1.4,
  ),
)

Font Loading Note

The Noto fonts are loaded via Google Fonts CDN in web/index.html:

frontend/web/index.html

Issue 4 — Assistant Language Control

Observed Symptom

The AI assistant always replied in the language it detected from the user's message (Hindi, Tamil, English), with no way for the user to force English responses.

Root Cause

The chat request schema (backend/app/schemas/chat.py) had no response_language field. The LLM service (backend/app/chat/service.py) relied entirely on implicit language detection from the user's input text. There was no mechanism to override this behavior.

Implicit vs Explicit Language Control

Implicit (before): LLM infers response language from user message language.
Explicit (after): UI language picker → API parameter → system prompt instruction → LLM responds in selected language.

Full Stack Changes

1. Backend Schema

backend/app/schemas/chat.py 
class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    message: str
    farm_id: Optional[int] = None
    crop_id: Optional[int] = None
    response_language: str = "en"  # NEW: default English

2. Backend Router

backend/app/chat/router.py 
@router.post("/send")
async def send_message(
    request: ChatRequest,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    conversation = await chat_service.create_pending(
        user_id=current_user.id,
        message=request.message,
        farm_id=request.farm_id,
        crop_id=request.crop_id,
        response_language=request.response_language,  # Pass through
        db=db,
    )
    # ...

3. Backend Service — Persist Language in Context

backend/app/chat/service.py 
async def create_pending(..., response_language: str = "en", ...):
    context_snapshot = {
        "response_language": response_language,
        # ... other context
    }
    pending = Conversation(
        # ...
        context_snapshot=json.dumps(context_snapshot),
    )

async def generate_and_persist(conversation_id: int, db: Session):
    conv = db.query(Conversation).get(conversation_id)
    context = json.loads(conv.context_snapshot or "{}")
    response_language = context.get("response_language", "en")
    response = await _generate_with_llm(conv.user_message, response_language)
    # ...

4. LLM System Prompt Injection

backend/app/chat/service.py 
async def _generate_with_llm(user_message: str, response_language: str) -> str:
    lang_names = {"en": "English", "hi": "Hindi", "ta": "Tamil"}
    lang_name = lang_names.get(response_language, "English")

    system_prompt = f"""You are an agricultural assistant for Indian farmers.
    ALWAYS respond in {lang_name}. Do not translate unless asked."""
    # ... call LLM with system_prompt

Cross-Cutting Themes & Lessons Learned

1. Configuration Drift Between Environments

All four issues stemmed from differences between local development assumptions and containerized deployment reality:

  • Networking: localhost means different things in host vs container vs browser contexts
  • Database: Migrations must be part of container lifecycle, not one-time local commands
  • Fonts: Web platform has different font stack than mobile/desktop
  • Language: Implicit behavior (auto-detect) differs from explicit user intent

2. Debugging Methodology

Effective debugging followed a consistent pattern:

  1. Check the actual network request (browser DevTools Network tab) — revealed HTML responses for API calls
  2. Read the full error stack trace — sqlite3.OperationalError pointed directly to missing column
  3. Inspect rendered output — empty boxes indicated font glyph missing, not empty string
  4. Trace data flow end-to-end — language parameter from UI → API → Service → LLM prompt

3. Docker Development Workflow

The docker-compose.dev.yml pattern with volume mounts enabled rapid iteration without full rebuilds:

  • Frontend source mounted → hot reload via Flutter web
  • Nginx config mounted → proxy changes instant
  • Backend source mounted → uvicorn --reload (if configured)

4. Defensive Frontend Practices

Added defensive coding in assistant_screen.dart:

Defensive rendering 
String? _normalizedText(String? text) {
  if (text == null) return null;
  final trimmed = text.trim();
  return trimmed.isEmpty ? null : trimmed;
}

// In _loadHistory():
final normalized = _normalizedText(msg.response);
if (normalized == null) {
  // Show error placeholder instead of empty bubble
  return _buildErrorPlaceholder(msg);
}

All fixes verified against the following criteria:

Database schema matches models ✅ Pass alembic current shows head revision
Hindi/Tamil text renders without boxes ✅ Pass Font fallback chain loaded; glyphs visible in chat
Default language is English ✅ Pass response_language: "en" sent when picker unchanged
Language picker changes response language ✅ Pass LLM system prompt includes selected language
Empty history messages don't create blank bubbles ✅ Pass Normalized text guard returns null for empty strings
